titulo: How a rotary engine works (real speed)
caption:
How do you build an engine without pistons?

A triangular rotor spins inside a peanut-shaped housing. Each face goes through intake, compression, combustion and exhaust. In the two-rotor Mazda Renesis, with a 9,000 RPM redline, that means 300 power pulses every second.

This is a pixel-art cutaway of the real mechanism. Follow the page for the next machine, and tell us which one you want explained next.
